acceptance_interpretation: Restoring the existing nightly selection is a quality-command contract repair. It does not establish a native Windows 10-second performance pass. Existing failures and actual future native results must remain distinct.

findings.evidence: M8-T04 requires slow performance tests in daily nightly, not per-PR. The performance test module states the same; the existing nightly runs tests/perf with -m slow without coverage.
findings.recommendation: Keep the 10/15-second tests and nightly execution unchanged; combine Windows normal-quality selection as not slow and not linux_only.

findings.evidence: Committed pyproject defaults -m not slow; committed Windows main quality command appends -m not linux_only. Later conflicting CLI options replace the configured marker expression.
The reported 17.1-second failure occurs with coverage instrumentation. It is retained as a real failure for that execution mode and cannot be relabeled as native uninstrumented performance.

Current Windows candidates retain full canonical target resolution. Python Windows lstat follows non-name-surrogate reparse points, so returned regular metadata cannot prove that the original leaf has no such reparse point.
